summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis and a history of failed kidney transplant was admitted with fevers, chills, and a diffuse itchy rash that began after receiving cefazolin at dialysis for presumed catheter site infection. Evaluation revealed no evidence of active infection, and blood cultures were negative. The symptoms were attributed to a systemic allergic reaction to cefazolin, consistent with his known allergy. He developed reactive arthritis with knee pain, confirmed by arthrocentesis showing no infection or gout crystals. During dialysis, he experienced a flare of rash and left hand swelling, which improved with IV hydrocortisone, famotidine, and diphenhydramine. Dermatology diagnosed a fixed drug eruption and recommended clobetasol cream. Prednisone was started, improving his joint symptoms. A urine culture grew Proteus mirabilis, but due to lack of symptoms and poor urine output, it was considered colonization and not treated. He stabilized, completed his hospital course, and was discharged home with a short course of prednisone, increased phosphate binder dose, and instructions for rash management and antibiotic avoidance.
problems: Dermatitis due to drugs and medicines taken internally
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Cephalosporin group causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
Surgical operation with transplant of whole organ causing abnormal patient reaction, or later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of operation
